source.citation: "Kinzie Mansion—1812." — halftone plate after Sarony's lithograph, in Joseph Kirkland, The Chicago Massacre of 1812 (Chicago: Dibble Publishing Co., 1893), p. 73.
what_it_does_not_supply: anything the Currey plate does not: it is the same artwork, cropped a little closer, and its 1812 caption is Kirkland's reading of it, not the artist's
what_it_supplies: the house long and low under a gable roof along the river, the east end toward the eye's right, a piazza across the front on posts with a rail
a picket fence round the green before the house down toward the water, a landing at the water's edge
four columnar Lombardy poplars in a row east of the house running toward the river, and a great broad-crowned tree behind it
two stacks through the ridge, and outbuildings and a two-storey house up the road to the west, behind the house
